title: Claude wrote all the code for my free browser kingdom game. No asset files: every sprite is drawn in code and every sound is synthesized
author: Immediate-Election-5
selftext:
Free to play here: [https://experiments.sandensolutions.com/emberhold/?ref=r-aigamedev](https://experiments.sandensolutions.com/emberhold/?ref=r-aigamedev) (no sign-up, no ads, keyboard or touch)

This is Emberhold, a side-scrolling kingdom game in the spirit of Kingdom Two Crowns (a fan homage, not affiliated with Raw Fury). You ride a stag as a little moss spirit, toss seeds to hire woodland townsfolk, turn them into archers, builders, farmers and knights, grow your walls and towers, and try to survive the nights when the rot comes out of the woods. Each later land has a beast you can ride instead of the stag (a lynx, a mossy bear, a salamander that breathes fire on the rot), and you can play solo or online co-op from the menu.

How the AI part works: I'm a solo dev and Claude wrote all of the code. I do the design, play it every day, and tell it what feels wrong. The part I think this sub will find most interesting is that there are no asset files at all. Every sprite (the stag's walk, the mice, foxes and badgers, the rot, the trees, the water) is drawn by code as pixel art, and every sound (arrows, the fire crackle, wind, the night drone) is synthesized live with WebAudio. When I want a new creature I describe it, Claude writes the drawing code, and I send notes until it reads right.

Things I've learned so far:

\- Asking for a whole system in one go always looked done until I played it. Small steps with a playtest after each one works way better.

\- Having it build test hooks into the game (fast forward the sim, spawn a raid, skip to night, run scripted inputs) means it can check its own work headless before I ever see it. This clip was recorded that way: the live build stepped frame by frame, with the game's own audio rendered offline.

\- Art made of code is slow to get right the first time, but cheap to change later. I recently switched the whole game over to this woodland look, and the rules underneath didn't move.

It's very much a work in progress. Happy to go into the workflow, and I'd love to hear where it feels off.
